Chapter:
Automizer Sequences
Let S be a p-group, with proto-essential subgroups E_1, \dots, E_n. An automizer sequence is a list P := [H_{i_1}, \dots, H_{i_k}], where H_{i_j} \leq \textrm{Aut}(E_{i_j}) is a valid automizer for E_{i_j} in S. In other words, \textrm{Aut}_S(E_{i_j}) is a Sylow p-subgroup of H_{i_j}), and H_{i_j}/\textrm{Inn}(E_{i_j}) contains a strongly p-embedded subgroup. Note that we do not include a choice of H_S \leq \textrm{Aut}(S) here. These are prototypes for saturated fusion systems. In this chapter, we describe processes to determine many important properties about automizer sequences that will allow us to determine whether the corresponding fusion system would be reduced. Note that the functionalities here are not guaranteed to be correct or complete just yet.
The functions
a list of valid Aut_F(E)
Let S be a p-group, and let L be a list of subgroups of S, all of which are proto-essential in S. We compute all possible automizer sequences involving the subgroups in L that could lead to reduced fusion systems.
an isomorphism mapping
Given two automizer sequences P_1 and P_2, check whether there exists some \phi \in \textrm{Aut}(S) such that P_1^\phi = P_2. This computation mimics isomorphism of fusion systems. The action of \phi is dependent of the ordering of the P_i's.
a list
Finds valid automizers for E in S. This is not part of the proto-essentials test and forms the first step in the actual construction of fusion systems. Nonetheless, if a subgroup is proto-essential, then it must have a valid automizer. This function does not construct all subgroups of \textrm{Aut}(E)/O_p(\textrm{Aut}(E)), and instead uses iterative maximal subgroup condition to do so.
a group
Let S be a p-group, and let E < S with some fixed H_E \leq \textrm{Aut}(E) part of an automizer sequence. The operation FindSmallestBorel computes the subgroup of \textrm{Aut}(S) consisting of extensions from N_{H_E}(\textrm{Aut}_S(E)). If not every map in the normalizer subgroup exists, we return fail.
true or false
Let S be a p-group, and let E < S with some fixed H_E \leq \textrm{Aut}(E) part of an automizer sequence. Let H_S \leq \textrm{Aut}(S) be a subgroup. The operation IsAutomizerBorelCompatible checks whether the restrictions of H_S are compatible with H_E. In particular, if A_0 \leq \textrm{Aut}(E) consists of restrictions from H_S, we have that O^{p'}(\langle A_0, H_E \rangle) = H_E.
true or false
Let S be a p-group and let P be an automizer sequence. The operation IsCompatibleSequence checks whether P can lead to a saturated fusion system. Note that there can be false positives -- P may not lead to a saturated fusion system (based on the analysis of centric, radical subgroups) but passes this test.
a record
Let S be a p-group and let P be an automizer sequence. If we set \mathcal{F} := \langle P \rangle, the operation OrbitStabilizerFusion returns a record R, storing:
\mathcal{F}-orbit A^{\mathcal{F}} (in R.orbit),
the isomorphisms \phi_i \colon A \to A_i for some A_i \in A^{\mathcal{F}} (in R.maps), and
the automizer \mathrm{Aut}_{\mathcal{F}}(A) (in R.AutFA).
The operation uses breadth-first search, where the vertices is the \mathcal{F}-orbit and the edges are the maps in P.
true or false
Let S be a p-group, W be a subgroup of S, and let P be an automizer sequence. The operation WeakRadicalCheck does a weaker version of the saturation check with respect to the possible centric-radical subgroup W. In particular, taking \mathcal{F} := \langle P \rangle, the function works as follows:
We start by computing the orbit W^\mathcal{F} and the stabilizer \mathrm{Aut}_{\mathcal{F}}(W).
We conjugate W so that it is fully \mathcal{F}-normalized.
We check that \mathrm{Aut}_S(W) is a Sylow p-subgroup of \mathrm{Aut}_{\mathcal{F}}(W).
If X is a subgroup of N_S(W) such that N_{\mathrm{Out}_{\mathcal{F}}(W)}(\mathrm{Out}_X(W))/\mathrm{Out}_X(W) has a strongly p-embedded subgroup, then
N_{\mathrm{Aut}_{\mathcal{F}}(W)}(\mathrm{Aut}_X(W)) = \mathrm{Aut}_{\mathrm{Aut}_{\mathcal{F}}(W)}(\mathrm{Aut}_X(W)). The function always returns true if W is not \mathcal{F}-centric or if there exists a \mathcal{F}-conjugate A of W satisfying: O_p(\mathrm{Aut}_{\mathcal{F}}(A))) \cap \mathrm{Aut}_S(E) > \mathrm{Inn}(E).
